# Cynefin diagram syntax

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-cynefin/grammar/cynefin.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

Cynefin diagram syntax (R-PARSE-9, D54): the normative grammar of `cynefin-beta` diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a reference
parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it. mermaid@12
decides what is valid, this file is fixed to match, and the parser must match this file
(DESIGN §4.4). mermaid@12 parsed cynefin with Langium (`cynefin.langium` and `common.langium`
in `@mermaid-js/parser`); the rules below are its token rules, in its order, and its grammar.

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; `%%` comment lines removed and leading blanks trimmed; on a line with
`style…:…#…;` (or `classDef…`) the last `;` dropped; `#name;` / `#123;` entities read as
opaque text; and a line break appended. Keywords and domain names are case-sensitive.

A domain's items follow its name, on the same line or on the lines after it; a transition, a
title and an accessibility statement each end at a line break (or the end of the text). `;`
is not a separator.

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

A diagram is `cynefin-beta`, then domain blocks, transitions and statements. A block's items
may share its line or follow on later lines, blank lines included; the other statements end at
a line break. The `YAML`, `DIRECTIVE` and `COMMENT` tokens of the lexer are skipped before
parsing.

```ebnf
cynefin = { NEWLINE } Header { NEWLINE | Domain | ended NEWLINE } [ ended ] EOF ;
```

```ebnf
Header @Header = HEADER
               | HEADER_COLON ;
```

```ebnf
ended = Transition
      | Title
      | AccTitle
      | AccDescr ;
```

`complex "Probe" "Sense"`: a domain (`complex`, `complicated`, `clear`, `chaotic` or
`confusion`) and its items, which may each be on a line of their own. Only the last block of a
domain is drawn, at the place of its first.

```ebnf
Domain @Domain = DOMAIN_NAME { { NEWLINE } Item } ;
```

`"Probe"`: an item of the domain before it.

```ebnf
Item @Item = STRING ;
```

`complex --> clear : "Pattern found"`: a transition and its optional label. A transition from
a domain to itself is not drawn.

```ebnf
Transition @Transition = DOMAIN_NAME ARROW DOMAIN_NAME [ COLON STRING ] ;
```

`title Incident response`: the title drawn above the diagram (the last one wins).

```ebnf
Title @Title = TITLE ;
```

`accTitle: …`: the accessible title.

```ebnf
AccTitle @AccTitle = ACC_TITLE ;
```

`accDescr: …` or `accDescr { … }`: the accessible description.

```ebnf
AccDescr @AccDescr = ACC_DESCR ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | HEADER_COLON | `cynefin-beta:` |  | `cynefin-beta:` starts a cynefin diagram, as `cynefin-beta` does; anything may follow the colon. |
| INITIAL | HEADER | `cynefin-beta(?:(?=%%)\|(?!\S))` |  | `cynefin-beta`: starts a cynefin diagram of the five domains. |
| INITIAL | ARROW | `-->` |  | `complex --> clear`: a transition from one domain to another. |
| INITIAL | COLON | `:` |  |  |
| INITIAL | DOMAIN_NAME | `complex\|complicated\|clear\|chaotic\|confusion` |  | A domain: `complex`, `complicated`, `clear`, `chaotic` or `confusion` (the centre, also called disorder). Its items follow it; a name repeated later replaces the earlier block's items. |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `[\t ]*accDescr[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accDescr: …` (the rest of the line) or `accDescr { … }` (over lines, to `}`): the accessible description of the diagram. mermaid@12's one rule, as two tried in order; the block's `[\s\S]*?\}` is its `[^}]*\}`, written so that line-based highlighters read the block as one span. |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `[\t ]*accDescr\s*\{[\s\S]*?\}` |  |  |
| INITIAL | ACC_TITLE | `[\t ]*accTitle[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accTitle: …`: the accessible title of the diagram, the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | TITLE | `[\t ]*title(?:[\t ][^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[\t ][^\n\r]*\|)` |  | `title …`: the title drawn above the diagram, the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | STRING | `"(?:[^"\\]\|\\.)*"\|'(?:[^'\\]\|\\.)*'` |  | An item of a domain, or the label of a transition: `"…"` or `'…'`; `\` escapes the next character, and a label may span lines. |
| INITIAL | NEWLINE | `\r?\n` |  |  |
| INITIAL | — | `[\t ]+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | YAML | `---[\t ]*\r?\n(?:[\S\s]*?\r?\n)?---(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A `---` … `---` block inside the body: skipped. |
| INITIAL | DIRECTIVE | `[\t ]*%%\{[\S\s]*?\}%%(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A `%%{…}%%` left in the text the lexer reads: skipped. |
| INITIAL | COMMENT | `[\t ]*%%[^\n\r]*` |  | `%%` to the end of the line, after other text: a comment. |
| INITIAL | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- COMMENT: `^[^\S\n]*%%(?!\{)[^\n]+`
- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
